title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Lawfully Adjudicating and Enforcing Civil and Commercial Cases to Ensure the Healthy Development of Private Investment
keywords_en: court trial and enforcement of civil and commercial cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Lawfully Adjudicating and Enforcing Civil and Commercial Cases to Ensure the Healthy Development of Private Investment

Fa [2016] No. 334

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Both the public-owned economy and the non-public-owned economy are important components of the socialist market economy and are important foundations for China's economic and social development. Promoting the healthy development of private investment benefits both the present and the long term, is of great significance for stabilizing growth and ensuring employment, and is also an important element of supply-side structural reform. People's courts at all levels must firmly establish the awareness of serving the overall situation and administering justice for the people, and deeply understand the importance of properly conducting civil and commercial adjudication work involving private investment under the current circumstances. In order to effectively carry out the civil and commercial adjudication work involving private investment, in accordance with relevant laws and national policies, the following issues that should be noted in judicial practice are hereby notified:

1. Actively implement the spirit of the Central Committee and lawfully ensure the healthy development of private investment.

The non-public-owned economy is an important foundation for stabilizing the economy, an important source of national tax revenue, an important entity for technological innovation, an important support for financial development, and an important force for sustained and healthy economic development. The Third, Fourth, and Fifth Plenary Sessions of the 18th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China put forward clear requirements for improving the property rights protection system and equally protecting all forms of ownership. General Secretary Xi Jinping emphasized that the state protects the property rights and legitimate interests of all forms of ownership, adheres to equality of rights, equality of opportunities, and equality of rules, and stimulates the vitality and creativity of the non-public-owned economy. Lawfully and equally protecting the non-public-owned economy and promoting the healthy development of private investment are important elements of supply-side structural reform. People's courts at all levels must thoroughly implement the spirit of the Central Committee, give full play to the role of civil and commercial adjudication functions, adhere to the six principles of protecting property rights, freedom of contract, equal protection, unity of rights, obligations and responsibilities, good faith, and unity of procedural justice and substantive justice, lawfully resolve various disputes in private investment, ensure the healthy development of private investment, and serve the five major developments of "innovation, coordination, greenness, openness, and sharing."

2. Unify strict law enforcement and equally protect the non-public-owned economy in accordance with the law.

Equality before the law is a fundamental principle established by China's Constitution. When adjudicating civil and commercial cases, people's courts at all levels must equally protect the legitimate rights and interests of the non-public-owned economy in accordance with the law, adhere to equality of litigation status, equality of application of law, and equality of legal liability for all market entities, and provide equal judicial protection for all forms of ownership. Adhere to equality of litigation status: entities of the public-owned economy and entities of the non-public-owned economy enjoy the same litigation rights and bear the same litigation obligations. Adhere to equality of application of law: entities of the public-owned economy and entities of the non-public-owned economy are subject to the same transaction rules, equally use production factors, and fairly participate in market competition. Adhere to equality of legal liability: both entities of the public-owned economy and entities of the non-public-owned economy must abide by the law, and those who violate the law shall bear legal liability in accordance with the law.

3. Lawfully and properly adjudicate contract dispute cases and protect lawful transactions.

Promptly adjudicate contract dispute cases related to private investment, such as sales, loans, construction, and processing contracts, correctly allocate the contractual responsibilities of the parties, and protect the legitimate rights of various investment entities. Correctly handle the relationship between party autonomy and administrative approval. For contracts that require approval, registration, or other formalities to become effective under laws and administrative regulations, efforts should be made to promote the validity of the contract to the greatest extent possible, in accordance with the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the PRC. Correctly understand, identify, and apply the "mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations" in Article 52, Item (5) of the Contract Law, pay attention to distinguishing between mandatory provisions relating to validity and mandatory provisions relating to management, and strictly limit the scope of invalidity determination. Where one party requests rescission of a contract, it shall strictly examine whether the conditions for rescission are met in accordance with Articles 93 and 94 of the Contract Law, to prevent a party acting in bad faith from evading debts through contract rescission.

4. Lawfully and properly adjudicate rights and interests dispute cases and protect legitimate investment interests.

Give full play to the civil and commercial adjudication functions, straighten out property rights relationships. While protecting the public-owned economy in accordance with the law and effectively preventing the loss of state-owned assets, it is also necessary to prevent improperly harming the legitimate rights of non-public-owned economic entities beyond the provisions of laws and contracts. For affiliated enterprises with disputed property rights, ownership must be clearly determined on the basis of carefully ascertaining the investment facts to prevent illegal encroachment on the property of non-public-owned economic entities. Strictly in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and policies, adjudicate enterprise restructuring dispute cases, accurately define property rights relationships, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of non-public-owned economic entities. Properly adjudicate cases involving overseas investment to ensure the implementation of the "going global" strategy by non-public-owned economic entities and expand foreign investment. Strictly in accordance with the Interpretation (III) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the PRC, properly adjudicate various shareholder qualification dispute cases, and lawfully protect the legitimate rights and interests of non-public-owned economic shareholders who have actually made capital contributions. Lawfully adjudicate disputes concerning shareholders' right to know, right to claim profit distribution, and claims for confirmation of invalidity or revocation of resolutions of the board of directors, shareholders' meeting, or general meeting of shareholders, and protect the shareholder rights of various investment entities. Through the adjudication of equity transfer dispute cases, smooth the channels for equity transfer, and lawfully protect the right of various investment entities to exit the company. When adjudicating cases where company creditors request the company to repay debts, lawfully distinguish between company property and the personal property of shareholders or family common property, correctly determine the liable property of the company, prevent using the personal property of shareholders and family common property to repay company debts without legal basis, and effectively protect the legitimate rights and interests of non-public-owned economic shareholders.

5. Lawfully and properly adjudicate intellectual property cases and strengthen intellectual property protection.

Fully utilize the means of judicial protection of intellectual property rights, and increase the punishment for various acts of intellectual property infringement. Properly adjudicate contract dispute cases concerning technology development, technology transfer, technology consultation, and technology services arising during the process of technological transformation and upgrading, encourage non-public-owned economic entities to achieve industrial upgrading through technological progress and technological innovation, and enhance core competitiveness. Promptly accept unfair competition dispute cases, lawfully sanction various forms of unfair competition acts, and ensure that non-public-owned economic entities participate in market competition on an equal footing. Strengthen the adjudication of antitrust cases, lawfully prevent monopolists occupying a dominant market position from abusing such dominance, strictly pursue legal liability for illegal monopolistic acts, and provide a competitive, efficient, and fair market environment for economic entities of all forms of ownership.

6. Lawfully and properly adjudicate financing dispute cases and alleviate difficulties and high costs in financing.

Lawfully adjudicate cases involving financial loans, financial leasing, private lending, etc., involving non-public-owned economic entities, and lawfully support the multi-channel financing of non-public-owned economic entities. In accordance with the latest developments in the principle of numerus clausus of property rights, correctly determine the legal validity of new types of security contracts, and help enhance the financing guarantee capacity of non-public-owned economic entities. Correctly understand and apply the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Adjudication of Private Lending Cases, within the framework of a unified and standardized financial system reform, lawfully protect private financial innovation, promote the orderly market-based flow of private capital, and alleviate the financing difficulties of small and micro enterprises. Strictly implement the judicial protection standards for lending interest rates, and do not support the disguised high interest charged by commercial banks, pawn companies, small loan companies, etc., through unreasonable fees other than interest. Distinguish between normal lending activities and illegal or criminal activities using loan funds. While lawfully combating and dealing with illegal fundraising crimes, it is also necessary to protect lawful lending activities and lawfully protect the legitimate rights and interests of contract parties. During case adjudication, if criminal suspicions such as money laundering, violent debt collection, or malicious debt collection caused by high interest rates are discovered, relevant materials must be promptly transferred to the public security authorities to promote the formation of a lawful and orderly private lending market.

7. Lawfully and properly adjudicate labor dispute cases and reduce enterprise labor costs.

Continue to adhere to the concept of equally protecting the legitimate rights and interests of workers and the survival and development of enterprises, adhere to the organic unity of protecting workers' rights and the survival and development of enterprises, strive to find a balance of interests, and combine the protection of workers' immediate and practical interests with the protection of their long-term and fundamental interests. Based on the specific circumstances of whether enterprises can adapt to market demands, carry out targeted adjudication of labor dispute cases and optimize the allocation of labor factors. For enterprises with temporary financial difficulties but development potential, especially small and micro enterprises, encourage workers and enterprises to tide over difficulties together through settlement, mediation, and other means. For enterprises forced to exit the market due to overcapacity, prevent employers from maliciously infringing upon workers' rights, strengthen adjudication, property preservation, and advance enforcement efforts, and maximize the protection of workers' rights. For industrial restructuring with significant regional or industry impact, formulate contingency plans for labor dispute handling in advance, and form a multi-level, all-round collaborative linkage mechanism and joint dispute resolution force. Protect various lawful forms of employment by enterprises, balance the interests of workers and enterprises, reduce enterprise labor costs, and improve the industrial competitiveness of enterprises. Lawfully protect the entrepreneurial rights of workers, guide workers to change their employment concepts, and promote the formation of a new mechanism where entrepreneurship drives employment.

8. Lawfully and prudently take compulsory measures and protect the normal production and operation of enterprises.

Treat economic entities of all forms of ownership equally, and do not differ in enforcement intensity or enforcement standards due to the different nature of ownership of the applicant for enforcement and the person subject to enforcement, and fairly and efficiently protect the legitimate rights and interests of the party acting in good faith. Relying on the informatization construction of enforcement work, gradually realize the query and sharing of enforcement information, and strive to solve the problems of difficulty in locating the person subject to enforcement and difficulty in discovering the property subject to enforcement. When taking enforcement measures such as property preservation, seizure, impoundment, freezing, and detention, pay attention to the objective reality that non-public-owned economic entities are relatively small in scale and have relatively low risk resistance. For persons subject to enforcement involved in lawsuits due to changes in the macroeconomic situation or adjustments in industrial policies, or who are unable to perform debts in a timely manner due to temporary difficulties in production and operation, strictly grasp the application conditions for property preservation and evidence preservation, prudently use compulsory measures such as detention, seizure, and freezing in accordance with the law, minimize any improper impact that may be caused to the normal production and operation activities of the enterprise, and maintain the operational stability of non-public-owned economic entities. If compulsory measures such as seizure, impoundment, or freezing are truly necessary, they must be carried out strictly in accordance with legal procedures, and, to the extent possible, necessary current assets and transaction accounts shall be reserved for the enterprise to minimize the adverse impact on the normal production and operation activities of the enterprise.

September 2, 2016
